name: Polyhedra
tagline: Compact in-memory and flash relational DBMS for embedded, telecom and SCADA systems, sold by Enea.
description: Polyhedra is a small-footprint relational database family aimed at OEMs building embedded and always-on control systems. Polyhedra IMDB keeps the working set in RAM with snapshot-plus-journal persistence and hot-standby failover, while Polyhedra Flash DBMS stores data in a flash file with shadow paging for devices like set-top boxes and picocells. Its distinctive feature is active queries: a client subscribes to a query and is pushed deltas when the result changes, which removes polling from SCADA-style applications, plus a trigger language (CL) and table inheritance. Developed in the UK from 1991 and owned by Sweden's Enea since 2001, it is still listed by Enea but is a niche, sales-led product with little public release activity.
statusNote: Still listed and sold by Enea, but there are no public release notes or roadmap in recent years; treat it as a legacy embedded product.

pricing.notes: OEM licensing through Enea sales; a freeware Polyhedra Lite edition was released in 2012.

scale.notes: Designed for RAM-resident datasets on a single node, with a hot-standby replica for availability rather than clustering.

strengths: Active queries push result-set changes to clients, eliminating polling in control systems
Small RAM and code footprint suited to embedded OEM hardware
Hot-standby replication for always-on telecom and industrial deployments
Historian module for capturing and archiving high-rate time-series samples
Standard SQL, ODBC and JDBC interfaces despite the embedded focus
weaknesses: Restricted transaction model: a transaction is a query, a schema change or a batch of writes
No clustering or load sharing; scaling is vertical with one standby
Closed, sales-led product with little public documentation, community or release cadence
useCases: SCADA and industrial control data repositories
Telecom network equipment configuration and state
Embedded devices needing a relational store in flash
Maintaining existing OEM products already built on Polyhedra
